# Score analysis: POC001 gallery (generated by tools/score_analysis.py)

**Mostly synthetic faces (DigiFace-1M) plus one consenting volunteer. Synthetic faces may not behave like real
ones, so this shows the method, not operational numbers. No accuracy claims.**

Model `r50-buffalo_l`; gallery of 49 enrolled references; 97 mated probes and
3 stranger probes (1 probes skipped: not exactly one face).

| Distribution | n | min | p5 | median | p95 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Genuine (probe vs own reference) | 97 | 0.293 | 0.364 | 0.572 | 0.739 | 0.807 |
| Impostor top-1 (best non-mate; = runner-up when the mate is enrolled) | 100 | 0.080 | 0.204 | 0.280 | 0.383 | 0.413 |
| Margin genuine - best non-mate (mated probes) | 97 | -0.053 | 0.076 | 0.286 | 0.504 | 0.580 |

Rank-1 errors (a non-mate scored higher than the mate): 1 of 97.

| T | impostor top-1 >= T (false match if the mate were absent) | genuine < T (NO_MATCH, manual) | genuine >= T but margin < 0.10 (AMBIGUOUS) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.35 | 13 of 100 | 2 of 97 | 8 |
| 0.44 | 0 of 100 | 16 of 97 | 1 |

**Proposed T = 0.44**: the highest impostor top-1 seen (0.413) plus a 0.02 safety gap, rounded up.
With 100 impostor searches and none above T, the rule of three gives only a rough 95% upper bound of
~3% per search for the false-match rate: far too few samples to calibrate anything. Production
sets T at a target FPIR over flight-sized galleries with the vendor's calibration and operational data.
